query: Which open metadata standards, ontologies and repositories (for chronologies, lithic databases, sedaDNA, proteomics and isotopes) should we commit to, and how will pre-registration of pipelines be structured?

response.query: Which open metadata standards, ontologies and repositories (for chronologies, lithic databases, sedaDNA, proteomics and isotopes) should we commit to, and how will pre-registration of pipelines be structured?
response.answer: Commit to mzIdentML for proteomics, ISA-TAB for metadata, and PSI-MI for interactions; pre-registration of pipelines should follow FAIR principles and use community standards.

results.title: (PDF) ms-data-core-api: An open-source, metadata-oriented library for computational proteomics
results.content: # ms-data-core-api: An open-source, metadata-oriented library for computational proteomics. The mzIdentML data standard for mass spectrometry-based proteomics results. A cross-platform toolkit for mass spectrometry and proteomics. A guide to the Proteomics Identifications Database proteomics data repository. YPED: An Integrated Bioinformatics Suite and Database for Mass Spectrometry-based Proteomics Research. The ms-data-core-api is a free, open-source library for developing computational proteomics tools and pipelines. The data model is based on controlled vocabularies/ontologies and captures the whole range of data types included in common proteomics experimental workflows, going from spectra to identifications to quantitative results. The library contains readers for three of the most used Proteomics Standards Initiative standard file formats: mzML, mzIdentML, and mzTab. In addition to mzML, it also supports other common mass spectra formats: dta, ms2, mgf, pkl, apl (text-based), mzXML and mzData (XML-based). results.title: Towards a sample metadata standard in public proteomics repositories - PMC
results.content: For every proteomics dataset we should capture at least three levels of metadata: (i) dataset description, (ii) the sample to data files related information, and (iii) standard data file formats (e.g. mzIdentML, mzML or mzTab). While the dataset description and standard data file formats are supported by all ProteomeXchange partners; the information regarding the sample to data files is mostly missing. Recently members of the European Bioinformatics Community for Mass Spectrometry (EuBIC) have created an open-source project called Sample to Data file format for Proteomics () to enable the standardization of sample metadata of public proteomics dataset. In proteomics, HUPO-PSI (the Human Proteome Organization Proteomics Standard Initiative) has created a set of standard file formats to store mass spectra, peptide evidences, expression values, and/or protein-protein interaction information, among other proteomics data types (7). These file formats not only contain the data (e.g. spectra) in a standardized representation but also information in a standardized representation but also additional metadata related to analysis tools, and settings (for example, search engine scores used to select specific peptide evidence. As a resource routinely re-analyzing public datasets, ProteomicsDB (8), captures for each sample in the database a minimum number of properties to describe the sample and the related experimental protocol such as tissue, digestion method or instrument (e.g. For every proteomics dataset we should capture at least three levels of metadata: (i) dataset description, (ii) the sample to data files related information; and (iii) standard data file formats (e.g. mzIdentML, mzML, or mzTab). However, a careful review of an existing proteomics dataset annotated in ISA-TAB (11) makes clear that not only a file format is needed, but most importantly, general guidelines about what information should be encoded in proteomics data repositories. Recently members of the European Bioinformatics Community for Mass Spectrometry (EuBIC -) have created an open-source project called Sample to Data file format for Proteomics () to enable the standardization of sample metadata on public proteomics datasets. The project aims to extend the sample to the data file format (Sample and Data Relationship Format - SDRF) from MAGE-TAB to represent mass spectrometry-based proteomics experiments.

# Ontologies for Metadata registration. However i am facing some issues on which i’d like some points of view. What i’d ideally like is to get a minimal metadata template in the MDE configuration. This of course can ideally be solved by using drop down menus and using ontologies, which can nicely be done using MDE. However, now the question remains which ontology to use, and how are we going to keep those up to date? EDAM for example has confocal microscopy at several places in their ontology, And for example light sheet is under point scanning techniques. FBbi has issues like that there are no (or hardly any) super resolution techniques,. Is there a way to collaborate on these things to make sure these ontologies keep updated (since both are now 3 years old). You can find the ontologies that IDR currently uses at IDR: Linked resources. I like the FBBI the most since this focusses on strategies and not neceserrily all the technical details of the microscope. Though i am convinced that also needs to be tackled i hope that the Quarep ontology will be handled on the microscope company side in the end. results.title: AI-readiness - HUPO Proteomics Standards Initiative
results.content: ## PSI-AI: Advancing AI-readiness of public proteomics data. The PSI AI readiness working group aims to bridge the gap between artificial intelligence and public proteomics data. The first is to make public proteomics data suitable for AI applications. The second is to support and standardize the use of AI in workflows that generate new data. We work toward these goals through the use of community standards and reproducible and accessible pipelines. All deliverables, collaborators and existing efforts will be mapped on psi-ai.org. Improve Metadata Accessibility :** We support the active and retro-active annotation of public proteomics datasets to enhance their discoverability and reusability in AI contexts. Enable Low-Barrier Reprocessing:** We promote the development and dissemination of lightweight, community-friendly workflows that support the transformation of raw proteomics data into machine learning-ready formats. Contribute to AI Standardization in Proteomics:** We collaborate on the development of frameworks for benchmarking AI models and on the integration of existing PSI standards into AI pipelines.
